# Results — Study 422 (Elder Ray) on real daily tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Dr Alexander
Elder's Bull/Bear Power on a 13-period EMA turned into a long/flat daily timing rule
(long when EMA13 rises and Bear Power is negative-but-rising; flat when the trend turns
down), entered with a one-day execution lag, net of costs — raced against buy-and-hold
and against the two obvious simpler benchmarks (a 200-day SMA filter and a bare EMA13
cross). Sharpe is annualised and **excess-of-cash** for every arm (rf = 0 here, so it is
excess-vs-excess on the same baseline); data is Yahoo daily **total-return** bars
(`auto_adjust=True`). As-of **2026-05-31** (last complete month; the partial June 2026 bar
is dropped).*

## The honest test — SPY, Elder-Ray long/flat (net, cost = 2 bps one-way × NAV)

| Arm | Net Sharpe | CAGR | Max DD | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Elder Ray (long/flat)** | **+0.126** | **+0.74%** | **−39.0%** | **+0.730** |
| Buy & hold | +0.650 | +10.90% | −55.2% | +4.364 |

- Elder Ray's net excess Sharpe is **+0.126**, HAC *t* = **+0.730** — far below the
  **t ≥ 2** bar. It is invested only **46.2%** of the time and turns over **~29.9** one-way
  round-trips/yr.
- It **trails buy-and-hold by a Sharpe of −0.524** and gives up almost all the return
  (+0.74%/yr vs +10.9%/yr) in exchange for a milder drawdown (−39% vs −55%). It is a
  risk-reducer, not a return engine.
- **Rotation placebo *p* = 0.991** — circularly rotating *when* the rule is invested
  against the fixed asset returns does **as well or better in 99% of draws**. The realised
  timing carries no edge; if anything it is on the wrong side of random.

## The decisive race — does the Bull/Bear Power detail beat the simplest filter? (SPY, net)

| Rule | Net Sharpe | CAGR | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **200-day SMA filter** (long when Close > 200d SMA) | **+0.731** | +8.36% | +4.516 |
| EMA13 cross (long when Close > EMA13) | +0.329 | +3.11% | +1.968 |
| **Elder Ray (long/flat)** | +0.126 | +0.74% | +0.730 |

A one-line 200-day SMA filter beats Elder Ray on **every** metric, and even a bare EMA13
cross — Elder Ray's own trend component, *without* the Bull/Bear Power oscillators — beats
it. The extra machinery subtracts value relative to the trend it rides on.

## Long/short variant (SPY, net cost = 2 bps)

| Arm | Net Sharpe | CAGR | HAC *t* | Time in market |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Elder Ray long/short | −0.129 | −1.13% | −0.737 | 15.1% |

Adding the symmetric short leg makes it worse — fighting an up-drifting market with shorts
is a reliable loser.

## Cost sweep (Elder long/flat, SPY)

| Round-trip cost | Net Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.189 | +1.108 |
| 1.0 bps | +0.157 | +0.919 |
| 2.0 bps | +0.126 | +0.730 |
| 5.0 bps | +0.030 | +0.172 |

Even at **zero cost** the HAC *t* is +1.11 — below the bar before a single cent of cost.
Costs are not the killer; the timing simply isn't informative.

## Panel (Elder long/flat, net cost = 2 bps)

| Ticker | Elder Sharpe | Buy-hold Sharpe | Δ vs hold | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | +0.126 | +0.650 | −0.524 | +0.730 |
| QQQ | +0.247 | +0.523 | −0.275 | +1.316 |
| IWM | +0.066 | +0.472 | −0.407 | +0.338 |
| EFA | +0.094 | +0.406 | −0.312 | +0.500 |

No tape clears HAC *t* = 2 (the best is GLD at +1.77), and every tape's Elder-Ray Sharpe
is **below** its buy-and-hold Sharpe.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's trend to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a tunable AR(1)
trend knob, the **same** Elder-Ray rule reverses verdict once a real trend is planted:

| Planted AR(1) trend (`edge`) | Elder Sharpe | Buy-hold Sharpe | Δ vs hold | HAC *t* | Placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | +0.021 | +0.440 | −0.419 | +0.099 | 0.894 |
| +0.20 (strong trend) | +0.919 | +0.418 | +0.501 | +3.853 | 0.002 |

With trend planted, Elder Ray beats buy-and-hold, clears HAC *t* > 3, and the rotation
placebo collapses to *p* = 0.002 — proving the harness **can** bank a real timing edge.
The real-tape `NONE` is therefore a statement about the **market** (modern equity tapes
lack enough persistent daily trend to reward this filter over a simpler one), not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** SPY net excess Sharpe +0.126, HAC *t* = +0.730 (< 2), rotation
  placebo *p* = 0.991. No panel tape clears *t* = 2 (best GLD +1.77). Even gross, *t* = 1.11.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Trails buy-and-hold by Sharpe −0.524 with ~30 one-way
  round-trips/yr; the long/short variant is outright negative. Sidesteps drawdown at the
  cost of nearly all the return.
- **Beats a plain SMA filter? — BUSTED.** A one-line 200-day filter (Sharpe +0.731) and
  even a bare EMA13 cross (+0.329) both beat the full Elder-Ray rule (+0.126). The Bull/Bear
  Power oscillators add no incremental timing value on these tapes.
